linguistic_propositions.proposition: A preposition-plus-genitive unit cannot constitute a complete utterance on its own; it requires an attachment host, and that host may be absent from the surface.
The unexpressed host of the opening formula admits several rival estimates - a verb, a nominal comment, or a verbal noun - and the tradition supplies no single settled choice.
The elision of the host is purposeful, leaving the formula applicable to any action rather than to one named action.
Fronting a detached accusative pronoun before its verb produces restriction rather than mere reordering.
Restriction has at least three carriers: fronting of an argument, the compound restrictive particle, and negation combined with exception.

A definite nominative noun followed by a preposition-plus-genitive unit and no verb forms a verbless clause whose comment is that unit; an alternative treats the nominative as a fronted comment with an unexpressed topic.
The two transmitted readings at Q 1:4 receive the same genitive parse and differ only in derivational template and therefore in sense; both are treated as authentic.
The Arabic grammatical tradition arose in order to protect recitation from case error.
A single case exponent can invert the proposition a sentence expresses (illustrated from Q 9:3).

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A clause containing no expressed and no estimable verb has a topic, not an agent; the agent label is licensed only by a verb.
The compound restrictive particle conveys restriction rather than plain emphasis, and its second element cancels the emphatic particle's accusative assignment so the following noun stays nominative.
A preposition-plus-genitive unit cannot itself occupy the comment slot of the frozen negative copula; the comment is an estimated accusative participle to which the unit attaches.
The estimated comment is realised as a generic existential participle.
The apodosis takes the linking particle when it cannot itself carry the jussive.
The linking particle is required in this instance specifically because the frozen negative copula produces a nominal-style structure.
The subordinating particle assigns accusative to the following noun, and the clause it heads is an interpreted verbal noun occupying an argument slot.
Both verbs of a conditional headed by the basic conditional particle stand in the jussive.
A case exponent in a prophetic report can decide a legal ruling.
Prophetic speech represents the purest register of Arabic and is therefore an exemplary object of grammatical analysis.
Ornate literary prose and chronicle prose present the same parsing demands as prophetic reports, so training on one transfers to the others.

instructional_purpose: Separates two registers of the standard written language and enumerates the grammatical features that distinguish them, so that a reader knows which cue - case exponent or constituent order - carries the functional load in a given text. It frames the difference as register and period variation rather than as correctness, and closes with a feature-by-feature comparison of a chronicle passage against a modern retelling of the same events.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The dual is deployed freely in the older register across nouns, verbs, relatives, and pronouns, while later usage frequently substitutes plural forms.
The energetic is built on the jussive stem by suffixing a heavy or a light nun.
The light nun is defective across parts of the paradigm where the heavy nun is available.
The energetic paradigm is marginal in contemporary usage: effectively unused in speech and uncommon even in formal writing (register-scoped claim).
Pausal delivery with a final sukun is a valid reading tradition and not a failure to inflect.
The modern preference for subject-initial order is attributable to contact with European languages and to the need for clarity when case is unrealised.
Classical constituent order is free because case exponents disambiguate function regardless of position.
The presence of the emphatic or subordinating particle in a classical text is a reliable signal that the following noun is accusative, whereas in a modern text the signal is less reliable.
The distinction between the two subordinators after a verb of saying (direct versus reported speech) is often blurred in later usage.

The lesson's constructed 'modern' counterparts include agreement mismatches - a dual quantifier with plural agreement, a dual noun with a plural relative, an oblique dual as subject of a plural verb - and are demonstration artefacts rather than attested forms.

instructional_purpose: Makes the Arabic grammatical metalanguage itself the object of study, on the argument that a reader who cannot decode the labels cannot use any classical commentary. Each label is presented with its ordinary-language sense as a mnemonic for its function, and the assembled set is then shown at work on the way commentaries parse the opening line of a pre-Islamic ode.
later_dependencies: reading commentary prose, which presupposes every label in this set
extracting grammatical claims from commentary into structured records
any hover or gloss layer that surfaces Arabic grammatical labels to a learner

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Each grammatical label is transparently motivated by the ordinary sense of the word chosen, so knowing the ordinary sense recovers the function.
The agent is assigned nominative and the object accusative so that the two roles are not confused with each other.
The second term of a construct chain is genitive regardless of the case the first term carries.
The circumstantial accusative is always accusative, always indefinite, and always derived.
The topic of a verbless clause must be definite or functionally definite.
The comment is nominative when it is a single word, and otherwise follows the rules of its own internal structure.
Case is assigned by a governor to a governed element, and every case exponent has a governor to account for it.
Specification follows numerals in a stated band, measures, comparatives, and expressions of praise or blame.
An attribute agrees with its head in case, gender, number, and definiteness.
The label set established in the foundational treatise is the terminology used across all classical commentary.
Arabic grammatical categories have no reliable English equivalents and must be learned on their own terms.

misleading_shortcuts: every grammatical label is etymologically transparent
the label set is uniform across the whole classical tradition
any accusative that is not an object is a circumstantial
the circumstantial can be identified by meaning alone without the agreement test
a governor can always be named for every exponent
an English gloss of the label is an adequate substitute for the Arabic category

instructional_purpose: Teaches the classical commentary as a genre with its own readable syntax: a recurring three-move block of lemma marker, gloss marker, and justification marker, applied recursively across a base text and stacked in layers of base text, commentary, and marginal super-commentary. The grammatical payload is preposition-sense assignment, worked through the partitive reading and its substitution test.
later_dependencies: reading grammar treatises together with their commentaries and marginal notes
extracting attributed claims from commentary prose into a repository without collapsing them into verdicts
any provenance-aware ingestion of classical grammatical material

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Classical commentary proceeds by a recurrent three-move sequence: quote the lemma, gloss it, then justify the gloss.
A preposition carries the partitive sense when a quantity word can be substituted for it without loss of sense.
Under the partitive reading the following noun remains genitive, because the word is still a preposition; only the semantic relation changes.
One preposition may receive two different sense assignments in the same commentary, offered in disjunction rather than adjudicated.
The agent of a passive is deleted because it is recoverable from context.
An attribute takes the case of the word it describes.
Placing a prepositional unit before the agent signals that the speaker foregrounds the fronted material.
The commentary formula is uniform across poetry, prophetic reports, scripture, grammar, law, and technical prose.
The sample commentaries in this lesson are composed as demonstrations - one is explicitly framed as how a scholar might comment - and are not transmitted from any named commentator.
The indefiniteness marker on a cognate accusative signals a specified rather than an unrestricted instance of the action.

misleading_shortcuts: the substitution diagnostic settles the sense of the preposition in every case
whatever follows the gloss marker is the meaning, so no further parse is needed
a justification marker guarantees the interpretation has been proved

the three-move block is the only commentary format in the tradition
material quoted after a lemma marker is the commentator's own assertion
